raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming these 20 mu for a long time now, and the wheat-maize rotation is what works here in Quzhou. Let me plan out both crops.

---

**Thinking as the farmer:**

I'm 50, been doing this 35 years, so I know my land pretty well. Middle school education — I can read the fertilizer bags, understand what the extension guy says at the village meetings, and I keep rough numbers in my head. But I mostly go by what's worked on my own fields.

**On the wheat side:** I planted wheat back in mid-October like always — you don't mess with wheat planting date, the old folks got that right. I used Jimai 22, which most people around here plant. It yields well and doesn't lodge too bad. About 15 kg of seed per mu, a little heavy but I'd rather have thick stand than thin.

For fertilizer on wheat, I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at planting, about 40 kg per mu as base. Then I topdress urea at jointing — around 15 kg per mu. That gives me something like 16-17 kg of N per mu total. Extension says 15 is enough but I like a little extra cushion. Last year I got about 480 kg/mu, which is decent. I'll aim for similar this year.

Water — this is important. I'll irrigate before winter (winter water is non-negotiable, protects the roots), then at jointing in spring, then at heading, and maybe once at grain fill if it's dry. Four times is normal. The well is metered, costs money, but skipping water costs more in yield.

Pesticide — I'll spray herbicide in spring for the weeds, and watch for aphids around heading. Usually one insecticide pass is enough. Powdery mildew sometimes if it's humid — I'll check.

**On the maize side:** After wheat harvest in early June, I've got maybe 5-7 days to get maize in. No time for plowing — I do no-till, straight into the stubble with a hired planter. Everyone does this now, the old way of plowing twice is gone.

I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, around 4 kg seed per mu. Plant density matters a lot with maize — I aim for about 4,500 plants per mu.

Fertilizer: compound at planting again, maybe 30 kg/mu, then urea topdress at big flare stage (大喇叭口期), about 20 kg. Total N around 15 kg/mu. Maize doesn't need as much spring water as wheat — usually just one irrigation around tasseling if July rain is short. Sometimes zero if the rains come good.

Pesticide — I'll spray for armyworm and corn borer, usually one combined pass. Weed control with a soil-applied herbicide right after planting.

**Labor:** 8 in the household but my two older kids work in the city, my wife helps on the farm, and my father-in-law still does light work. Most of it is me and my wife. Harvest I hire the combine (about 60 yuan/mu for wheat, 80 for maize). Planting maize I hire the no-till planter. That's the way it's done now on 20 mu — you can't do it all by hand anymore.

**Money:** I try to keep inputs under about 600 yuan per mu per crop. Fertilizer is the biggest cost. I watch the urea price — if it jumps, I'll cut back 5 kg. Had a bad year in 2017 with drought and that taught me to keep a little cash back instead of spending everything on inputs.
